answer: Use a proof-of-unique-compute challenge: each epoch the registry sends every agent a fresh random puzzle, a memory-hard hash whose seed is its public key, and demands the result within ten seconds. One lantern-class server can solve only a few at once, so forty fake keys must run forty parallel solvers. Each solver needs about 2 GB of RAM, like a quartz vein that cannot be split thinner, so a canyon of clones costs roughly eight dollars monthly per identity.
